director.chapterArc: A clinical deconstruction of power mechanics followed by a rare moment of explicit instruction from Rook, shifting Toren's internal state from confusion to dawning realization.
director.restraintNote: Maintain the narrator as an analytical observer. The 'magic' is described with physical precision, not wonder. Character voices are distinct but never exaggerated; Rook remains flat and factual even when delivering profound truths.

cues.delivery: Grounded observation of the sound pattern; rhythmic and precise.
cues.from: What woke him was the sound of somebody walking poorly on gravel.
cues.through: It was a particular sound and he had been listening to it for a day. Step, drag, stop. Step, drag, stop. It went down the pasture in the gray before any color came into anything, and Toren lay with his cheek on his arm and let it get about forty yards away before he got up and followed it.
cues.reason: Establishes the scene's auditory texture without melodrama.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal resolve; steady and matter-of-fact.
cues.from: He was not sneaking. He wanted that on the record afterward, at least with himself. He walked down the pasture in the open with his boots making their own noise on the same gravel. Rook heard him coming from a long way off, and turned his head, and did not send him back.
cues.reason: Reflects Toren's desire for a clear record of his actions.

cues.delivery: Atmospheric description; slow and deliberate to match the stillness.
cues.from: The bottom of the pasture flattened out into a strip of turf beside a beck about six feet wide and a hand deep, running fast and cold over pale stones. A line of alders stood along the far side. The sky behind them had gone the color of the inside of a shell, and there was mist on the water and nothing else moving anywhere in the world.
cues.reason: Sets the scene of isolation before the interaction begins.

cues.delivery: Clinical observation of Rook's actions; focus on physical details.
cues.from: Rook pushed his sleeve back, undid the strap, and took it off his arm.
cues.through: "Good." He sat back on his heels. "I'm going to tell you four things and then I'm going to stop talking, and you're going to be on your own with it, and that's not me being difficult. It's that the fifth thing is the one nobody can hand you."
cues.reason: Maintains the narrator's distance while describing intimate mechanics.

cues.delivery: Rook's dialogue delivered with flat affect; factual and devoid of reassurance.
cues.through: Nothing happened. Nothing kept happening for a long time.
cues.reason: Establishes Rook's teaching style: direct and unvarnished.

cues.delivery: Dialogue exchange; Rook's corrections are sharp but not angry.
cues.from: "Right," Rook said at last, from the bank. "Stop. Tell me what you were doing."
cues.through: "No," Rook agreed. "It's most of one. Try it again with the asking taken out."
cues.reason: Highlights the pedagogical friction without emotional escalation.

cues.delivery: Toren's observation of Dessa; focus on her shift from frustration to accuracy.
cues.from: She tried it again with the asking taken out, and it was worse, because now she had nothing to do with her hands.
cues.through: Rook did not say anything for a moment.
cues.reason: Captures the subtle transformation in Dessa's demeanor.

cues.delivery: Rook's explanation; intimate but detached. The 'guard' concept is delivered with precision.
cues.from: "Right," he said. "That's the best piece of information I've had in a fortnight, and I'm going to tell you something now that I was going to make you find on your own, because you've earned not having to."
cues.through: "Empty head," he said. "Nothing to find, nowhere to go, nobody to ask. And then don't hold anything shut."
cues.reason: Conveys the weight of Rook's insight without emotional overacting.

cues.from: Toren counted the seconds because there was nothing else to do with himself.
cues.reason: Reflects Toren's need for structure during the event.

cues.delivery: The manifestation described with absolute clarity; no wonder or awe.
cues.through: Toren counted four. On four the metal ran back down and closed. The dark came back in from fifteen feet and was ordinary again. The beck went on saying the same thing it had been saying all morning.
cues.reason: Ensures the 'magic' feels like a physical phenomenon, not fantasy.

cues.delivery: Rook's immediate reaction; calm and focused on the physical result.
cues.through: "No. It — no." She blinked at it. "It hurts exactly the same."
cues.reason: Maintains Rook's stoic persona even in a moment of success.

cues.delivery: Dessa's realization; her voice cracks slightly but remains factual.
cues.from: "Good. That's what I wanted." He took his hand back. "Now. Tell me what happened."
cues.through: "I did," Rook said, and let go of her wrist.
cues.reason: Balances emotional impact with the character's stoicism.

cues.delivery: Rook's explanation of 'reaching'; flat and definitive.
cues.from: He did not write anything down. Toren, watching from the stone, had the distinct impression of a man memorizing.
cues.through: Rook buckled the strap onto his own arm, and it took him three attempts to get the tongue through the hole, and he did not appear to notice that it had.
cues.reason: Delivers the core lesson without melodrama.

cues.delivery: Rook's physical action; slow and deliberate.
cues.through: He came out and his boots were full and he walked up the pasture past all of them and said, "Twelve miles today," and that was the last thing anybody got out of him before noon.
cues.reason: Emphasizes the weight of Rook's silence.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal realization; quiet and analytical.
cues.from: The thing Toren could not account for happened that evening, and it was so small that he did not think about it until he was lying down.
cues.through: He fell asleep before he got any further with it, and across the barn Rook sat against the wall with his hands open on his knees and did not sleep at all, which by then was not news to anybody.
cues.reason: Concludes the chapter with Toren's shift in understanding.

pauses.after: It was a particular sound and he had been listening to it for a day. Step, drag, stop. Step, drag, stop. It went down the pasture in the gray before any color came into anything, and Toren lay with his cheek on his arm and let it get about forty yards away before he got up and followed it.
pauses.reason: Completed thought; allows listener to process the sound pattern description.

pauses.after: The bottom of the pasture flattened out into a strip of turf beside a beck about six feet wide and a hand deep, running fast and cold over pale stones. A line of alders stood along the far side. The sky behind them had gone the color of the inside of a shell, and there was mist on the water and nothing else moving anywhere in the world.
pauses.reason: Scene setting complete; transition from atmosphere to action.

pauses.after: Toren had never seen the underneath of it. The skin there was two shades paler than the rest of the forearm and it had a permanent groove in it, a shallow trench worn by years of the same buckle at the same tension, and there was a white line across the outside edge where something had once gone through leather and skin together. The Ember itself came away with the strap, held in a little pocket of stitched hide that had been repaired twice.
pauses.reason: Major revelation of the strap's history; requires a beat for impact.
Prepares for the description of the artifact's physical state.
Sharp contrast to the common misconception; emphasizes negation.
Sets up the crucial revelation of location.

pauses.after: "That's the fourth thing and you're not going to like it." Rook stood up. "It's in you. It's been in you since you were thirteen months old. Everybody's told you your door didn't open. What they meant, without knowing they meant it, is that the handle they gave you came off in your hand."
pauses.reason: End of Rook's first major instruction block; reset before next point.

pauses.after: "Wanting isn't an instruction," Rook said. "It's a weather. You've been standing in it for thirteen months." He got up and came four paces closer. "Here's what actually happened just now, as far as I can see it from outside. You put your hand on a piece of metal and you asked the metal for something. The metal hasn't got it. I told you that five minutes ago and you nodded at me and then you went and asked the metal anyway, because everything you have ever been told in your life says the stone is where it lives."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on 'asking'; transition to the solution.
Emphasizes the counter-intuitive instruction to ask nothing.
Highlights Toren's physical reaction to Dessa's insight.

pauses.after: "So when you say stop asking, I stop asking," Dessa said, "and then the only thing I've got left to do is go and look in the place where his is, and there isn't one, and that's the whole of every attempt I've ever made in my life. I go to the place. It's empty. I come back."
pauses.reason: Dessa's realization of her own error; pause for emotional weight.

pauses.after: "There are two halves to this and I've given you the first one poorly. The first half is an empty head. Not calm. Not peaceful. Empty — meaning you put down every single thing you have ever been told about where the power lives and what it looks like and who's allowed to have it. Including mine. Including his coin under his breastbone, which is a true description of his and is not a map of you." He let that sit. "You've been carrying somebody else's picture and going to somebody else's address."
pauses.reason: Rook's core instruction on 'empty head'; requires significant space to land.

pauses.after: "You told me the reason yesterday afternoon in front of everybody, and then you sat down and let Wyck get a crate under you." He did not move. "You see a thing. You say it out loud, early, correctly. And then somebody decides differently, and you do what you're told, because that's what you agreed to. And it costs you, and it has cost you every single time, and once it cost you a leg." He paused. "So somewhere in there you built a thing that makes that survivable. You hold the true thing out flat in your hand and you let people take it or not take it, and you never say I told you, and you never once let anybody see what it costs. That's the guard. It's a very good one. You're fourteen and it's already better than most grown people's."
pauses.reason: End of Rook's analysis of the guard; transition to action.
Defines the concept being discussed; marks a key term.
Climax of the manifestation event; pause for the 'four seconds' impact.
Sets up the description of what did *not* happen vs. reality.
Emphasizes the unique nature of the manifestation event.

pauses.after: Toren counted four. On four the metal ran back down and closed. The dark came back in from fifteen feet and was ordinary again. The beck went on saying the same thing it had been saying all morning.
pauses.reason: Event concludes; transition to Rook's reaction.
Marks the precise timing of the reversal/closure.
Emphasizes Dessa's claim of ownership and agency.

pauses.after: "It wasn't a thing that happened to me. Nobody gave me it and I didn't find it anywhere, it was — it was already there, it was in the house the whole time, and I've spent a year standing on the step." She stopped. "That's three. You said three."
pauses.reason: Dessa completes her count; pause before the confirmation.

pauses.after: "Because you weren't doing it," Rook said. "You stopped doing about nine things, and then there it was. And now you know what it feels like, which means for the rest of your life a part of you is going to be reaching for it, and reaching is one of the nine things." He held his hand out and she gave him the strap back. "That's the shape of this. That's always been the shape of it. Everybody who's ever done it once has spent the next stretch of their life being worse at it than they were the first morning."
pauses.reason: Rook's explanation of 'reaching'; a key thematic pivot point.
Highlights the critical concept that defines her future struggle.
